lines.text: 33. A liquid of density 600 kg/m’ flowing steadily in a
tube of varying cross-section. The cross-section at
a point A is 1.0 cm’ and that at B is 20 mm’. Both
the points A and B are in same horizontal plane,
the speed of the liquid at A is 10 cm/s. The
difference is pressures at A and B points is
34. A spherical liquid drop of radius R acquires the
terminal velocity v, when falls through a gas of
viscosity n. Now the drop is broken into 64
identical droplets and each droplet acquires
terminal velocity v, falling through the same gas.
The ratio of terminal velocities v,/v, is :
35. One mole of diatomic gas having rotational modes
only is kept is a cylinder with a piston system.
The cross-section area of the cylinder is 4 cm’.
The gas is heated slowly to raise the temperature
by 1.2 °C during which the piston moves by
25 mm. The amount of heat supplied to the gas is
R= 8.3 J/mol.K) (Neglect mass of the piston)
